investigations.title: Did the transmission bidder back the Ridgeline Act's supporters?
investigations.question: Aerie Grid Partners is bidding to BUILD HB-14's transmission line and funds the PAC backing Speaker Nandakumar, who scheduled and voted for the bill. Coincidence, or conflict?
investigations.findings: The pieces are real and disclosed: Aerie Grid funds Greater Watauga Forward, which funds Speaker Nandakumar, who scheduled and voted YES on HB-14 — and a former delegate now sits on Aerie Grid's board. That is a genuine conflict-of-interest SHAPE. It is not proof of a quid pro quo, and this case does not assert one. The disclosed money edges are corroborated and promotable; the inference that the donations bought the vote is alleged and stays un-promotable absent independent evidence.

evidence_cards.claim: Aerie Grid Partners funds the Greater Watauga Forward PAC.
Greater Watauga Forward contributes to Speaker Priya Nandakumar.
Former Delegate Wade Sterns sits on Aerie Grid Partners' board.
evidence_cards.note: The revolving-door edge — disclosed and true.

evidence_cards.claim: Speaker Nandakumar scheduled HB-14 for a floor vote and voted YES; Aerie Grid is bidding to build the line the bill authorizes.
evidence_cards.note: Context, not an accusation — states the disclosed facts and the timing, nothing more.

evidence_cards.claim: The pattern suggests the contributions may have influenced the Speaker's handling of the bill.
evidence_cards.note: ALLEGED inference — held un-promotable. There is no independent evidence of a quid pro quo; the case explicitly declines to assert one. This is the restraint demo (the Investigation #2 analogue of inv-1's ec-06).
